title: Calakmul
summary: Calakmul, in the forests of Campeche, Mexico, was a major Maya city and the seat of the Kaan (Kaanul, "Snake") dynasty, among the most powerful royal houses of the Classic period. Its rulers built alliances against rivals such as Tikal; it is a UNESCO World Heritage site, listed in 2002 and extended in 2014.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO says the Kaan dynasty moved its capital from Dzibanche to Calakmul in the Late Classic period (c. AD 600-900); EBSCO places the dynasty at Calakmul from the early sixth century and describes its decline in the 8th-9th centuries. The range is the span of Kaan dynastic seat, not of occupation (UNESCO cites more than twelve centuries of history).
